title: Implementation Science — Why Good Evidence Does Not Reach Patients

hook.en: Studies suggest it can take well over a decade for a proven treatment to become routine care, and many patients never get it. Knowing what works is only half the job. The other half is getting it done, and that is a science of its own.
hook.ur: Studies batati hain ke sabit shuda ilaaj ko routine care banne mein dehai se zyada lag sakti hai, aur bohat se mareez ko kabhi nahi milta. Yeh jaanna ke kya kaam karta hai aadha kaam hai. Doosra aadha usay karna hai, aur woh apni science hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name common barriers to using evidence (knowledge, attitude, time, resources, system), match each with a strategy, use the CFIR domains to think about a change in your clinic, and plan a small implementation project.
goal.ur: End tak aap saboot istemal karne ki aam rukawatein (ilm, rawaiyya, waqt, wasail, nizam) batayenge, har ek ko hikmat-e-amli se milayenge, apne clinic ki tabdeeli ke baare mein sochne ke liye CFIR ke domains istemal karenge, aur chhota implementation project plan karenge.

text.en: **Implementation science** studies how to get evidence-based practices into routine use. **Barriers** can sit at several levels: the **individual** (knowledge, habits, belief), the **team** (culture, leadership), the **organisation** (time, space, equipment, payment) and the **system** (policy, training, referral routes). Good implementation starts by **diagnosing** the barriers, then matches **strategies** to them: training, reminders, champions, audit and feedback, changes to forms and workflows. A single leaflet or lecture rarely changes behaviour.
text.ur: **Implementation science** parakhti hai ke saboot par mabni practices ko routine istemal mein kaise laya jaye. **Rukawatein** kai satahon par ho sakti hain: **shakhs** (ilm, aadatein, yaqeen), **team** (saqafat, qiyadat), **idara** (waqt, jagah, saman, adaigi) aur **nizam** (policy, training, refer ke raaste). Achha implementation pehle rukawaton ki **tashkhees** se shuru hota hai, phir un se **hikmat-e-amli** milata hai: training, yaad dahaniyan, champions, audit aur feedback, forms aur workflow mein tabdeeliyan. Ek leaflet ya lecture shayad hi rawaiyya badalta hai.

text.en: Think of **a new road**. Building the road (producing the evidence) is not enough. If the signposts are missing, the junction is dangerous or drivers do not know it exists, nobody will use it. Implementation is the signposts, the training and the habits that bring traffic to the road.
text.ur: **Nayi sadak** sochein. Sadak banana (saboot paida karna) kaafi nahi. Agar signboard na hon, mor khatarnak ho ya driver ko pata hi na ho to koi istemal nahi karega. Implementation signboard, training aur woh aadatein hain jo traffic ko sadak par laati hain.

question.en: A guideline recommends using a validated outcome measure at every first visit. Therapists know about it and agree, yet only 20 percent do it. What is the most likely barrier?
question.ur: Guideline har pehli visit par validated outcome measure istemal karne ki sifarish karti hai. Therapists ko pata hai aur woh mutafiq hain, phir bhi sirf 20 fisad karte hain. Sab se mumkina rukawat kya hai?

text.en: Lack of knowledge, so another lecture will fix it
text.ur: Ilm ki kami, isliye ek aur lecture theek karega

text.en: Therapists do not care about patients
text.ur: Therapists mareezon ki parwah nahi karte

feedback.en: There is no evidence of that.

text.en: Workflow and time barriers, so the form and routine need changing, not more lectures
text.ur: Workflow aur waqt ki rukawat, isliye form aur routine badalne ki zaroorat hai, mazeed lectures ki nahi

feedback.en: Yes — when people know and agree but do not do it, look at the system.
feedback.ur: Haan — jab log jaante aur mutafiq hon lekin na karein to nizam dekhein.

question.en: Why is a single leaflet or lecture usually not enough to change practice?
question.ur: Ek leaflet ya lecture aam taur par practice badalne ke liye kaafi kyun nahi?

text.en: Behaviour is shaped by habits, context and systems as well as knowledge, so several matched strategies work better
text.ur: Rawaiyya ilm ke saath aadaton, context aur nizam se banta hai, isliye kai munasib hikmat-e-amliyan behtar kaam karti hain

feedback.en: Yes — multifaceted strategies tend to work better.
feedback.ur: Haan — kai pehlu wali hikmat-e-amliyan behtar kaam karti hain.

question.en: Which is the best first step when you want to introduce a new routine in your clinic?
question.ur: Apne clinic mein nayi routine shuru karna chahte hon to behtareen pehla qadam kaun sa hai?

feedback.ur: Intezar mareezon ke faide mein der karta hai.

text.en: Find out the barriers and enablers by talking to the team and patients, then try a small pilot
text.ur: Team aur mareezon se baat kar ke rukawatein aur madadgar cheezein dhoondhein, phir chhota pilot aazmayein

feedback.en: Yes — diagnose first, then test small.
feedback.ur: Haan — pehle tashkhees, phir chhota test.

text.en: Announce it to everyone and expect them to follow
text.ur: Sab ko elaan kar dein aur follow karne ki umeed rakhein

feedback.ur: Yeh rukawaton ko nazar-andaaz karta hai.

text.en: **Blaming people for system problems.** "They just do not want to change" is rarely the real reason. Time, forms, space, patients' circumstances and leadership matter, and the first step is to listen. Another trap is trying to change everything at once; choose one practice, one team and one measure, learn from it and then spread.
text.ur: **Nizam ke masail ka ilzam logon par dena.** "Woh badalna hi nahi chahte" shayad hi asal wajah hoti hai. Waqt, forms, jagah, mareezon ke halaat aur qiyadat ahem hain, aur pehla qadam sunna hai. Ek aur jaal sab kuch ek saath badalne ki koshish hai; ek practice, ek team aur ek naap chunein, us se seekhein aur phir phailayein.

text.en: **Find a champion and start small.** One enthusiastic colleague, a one-page protocol and a two-week trial make a better start than a long policy. Show results quickly, such as "we measured 18 of 20 patients this fortnight", and celebrate progress. In Pakistan, work with senior clinicians and with administrators, who can remove practical barriers.
text.ur: **Champion dhoondhein aur chhote se shuru karein.** Ek josheela saathi, ek safha ka protocol aur do haftay ka trial lambi policy se behtar aaghaz hain. Nateeje jaldi dikhayein, jaise "is pakhwaray mein 20 mein se 18 mareezon ko naapa", aur pesh-raft ka jashn manayein. Pakistan mein senior clinicians aur intizamiya ke saath kaam karein, jo amali rukawatein door kar sakte hain.

question.ur: Kya implementation research se mukhtalif hai?

answer.en: Yes. Efficacy research asks whether a treatment works under controlled conditions. Implementation research asks how to get it used and whether it still works in routine care. Hybrid designs test both together. A treatment that works in a trial can fail in real life if nobody can deliver it, and implementation science is how we find out why.
answer.ur: Haan. Efficacy research poochhti hai ke ilaaj control shuda halaat mein kaam karta hai ya nahi. Implementation research poochhti hai ke isay istemal mein kaise laya jaye aur kya woh routine care mein phir bhi kaam karta hai. Hybrid designs dono ko saath aazmate hain. Jo ilaaj trial mein kaam kare woh haqeeqi zindagi mein nakam ho sakta hai agar koi usay de na sake, aur implementation science se hum wajah dhoondhte hain.

beats.patient: A hospital has an evidence-based falls prevention exercise programme, but only 30 percent of eligible older patients are referred. Staff say they forget, and the referral form is on a separate system.
beats.assessment: Barriers are not knowledge or attitude but workflow and the form.
beats.treatment: They add an automatic prompt to the discharge checklist, assign a nurse champion and give monthly feedback on referral numbers.
beats.reassess: Referrals rise from 30 to 70 percent within four months, and fewer patients return with falls.

text.en: **A new routine must not add risk.** When changing practice, check that the change does not remove a safety step, overload staff or exclude vulnerable patients. Track harm indicators along with progress, and be ready to pause or reverse the change if problems appear.
text.ur: **Nayi routine khatra na barhaye.** Practice badalte waqt dekhein ke tabdeeli safety ka qadam na hataye, staff par bojh na daale ya kamzor mareezon ko khaarij na kare. Pesh-raft ke saath nuqsan ke indicators bhi dekhein, aur masail ayen to tabdeeli rokne ya ulta karne ke liye tayyar rahein.

text.en: Grol and Grimshaw reviewed evidence on implementing change in patient care and concluded that no single strategy works everywhere; strategies should be matched to identified barriers, and approaches combining several methods, such as educational outreach, reminders and audit with feedback, are generally modestly effective. The CFIR framework organises factors that affect implementation into domains such as the intervention itself, the outer setting, the inner setting, the individuals involved and the process of implementation.
text.ur: Grol aur Grimshaw ne mareezon ki care mein tabdeeli ke implementation par saboot ka jaiza liya aur nateeja nikala ke koi ek hikmat-e-amli har jagah kaam nahi karti; hikmat-e-amliyan pehchani gayi rukawaton se milani chahiyen, aur kai tareeqe milane wale approaches, jaise taleemi outreach, yaad dahaniyan aur feedback ke saath audit, aam taur par maamooli mu'assir hain. CFIR framework implementation ko mutasir karne wale factors ko domains mein tarteeb deta hai, jaise intervention khud, bairooni mahaul, andar ka mahaul, shamil afraad aur implementation ka amal.

text.en: **Diagnose, Match, Pilot, Spread.** Diagnose the barriers, match strategies, pilot small and then spread.
text.ur: **Tashkhees, Milaap, Pilot, Phailao.** Rukawaton ki tashkhees, hikmat-e-amli ka milaap, chhota pilot aur phir phailao.

summary.en: Good evidence often fails to reach patients because of barriers at the individual, team, organisation and system levels.
summary.ur: Achha saboot aksar mareezon tak is liye nahi pohanchta ke shakhs, team, idara aur nizam ki satahon par rukawatein hoti hain.

summary.en: Diagnose the barriers, match strategies to them and pilot small before spreading.
summary.ur: Rukawaton ki tashkhees karein, hikmat-e-amli milayein aur phailane se pehle chhota pilot karein.

summary.en: Do not blame people for system problems, and check that changes do not add risk.
summary.ur: Nizam ke masail ka ilzam logon par na dein, aur dekhein ke tabdeeliyan khatra na barhayen.

front.en: What is a barrier to implementation?

back.en: Anything that prevents evidence-based practice from being used routinely.
back.ur: Har woh cheez jo saboot par mabni practice ko routine mein istemal hone se rokti hai.

front.en: Is one lecture usually enough to change practice?
front.ur: Kya ek lecture aam taur par practice badalne ke liye kaafi hai?

back.en: No; behaviour needs several matched strategies.
back.ur: Nahi; rawaiyye ko kai munasib hikmat-e-amliyan chahiye.

back.en: A colleague who enthusiastically promotes and supports a new practice.
back.ur: Saathi jo josh se nayi practice ko promote aur support kare.

note.en: Audit and feedback as an implementation strategy.
note.ur: Audit aur feedback implementation ki hikmat-e-amli ke taur par.
